uncertainty.description: Sample assumptions only. Edit and review them before using the numerical ranking for your own decision.

evidence.label: Unreviewed sample scenario assumptions
evidence.source: Explicit criterion scores and uncertainty spreads supplied in scenario_inputs. Missing sample inputs use neutral 0.5 scores.
evidence.population: Individual decision assumptions; no survey sample

assumptions: Criterion satisfaction uses a 0–1 scale; 1 means fully satisfies the stated value.
Five user weights sum to one. Years 1, 5 and 20 receive equal weight; there is no discounting.
Three hypothetical shared states have equal assumed probability, not empirically estimated probability. Each criterion is shifted by minus spread, zero, or plus spread and clipped to [0,1].
A state affects every option in the same direction, with an option-specific spread. This is an explicit dependence assumption.
Regret compares full-path utility against the best feasible fixed path within each state. Horizon bars compare options separately at that horizon, so their average need not equal full-path regret.
Upper-tail CVaR uses alpha=0.90; with three equally likely states this equals the worst state regret.
No life-outcome probability, causal estimate, statistical confidence interval, or convergence claim is produced.
method: Utility = weighted criterion satisfaction, averaged over horizons. Regret = best feasible full-path utility minus path utility in each shared state. Score = expected utility − risk_aversion × CVaR90(regret).
